articles.title: GTA 6’s Astonishing $4 Billion Day One Includes 32.5 Million Copies Sold
articles.title_tr: GTA 6’s Astonishing $4 Billion Day One Includes 32.5 Million Copies Sold
articles.summary:
GTA 6 is an enormous hit--it's the biggest gaming release ever. Take-Two just announced that GTA 6 reach 32.5 million copies sold before release, with revenue reaching $3.79 billion through the end of the first day on sale on November 19. This makes it the biggest entertainment release--for any medium--in history, Take-Two said.



For comparison, 2013's GTA 5 hit $800 million in revenue in its first 24 hours and $1 billion after its first three days, so GTA 6 is pacing well ahead of those numbers.



“It is with immense gratitude that we enter a new chapter of Rockstar Gameswith the release of Grand Theft Auto VI,” Rockstar president and co-founder Sam Houser said. “We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn’t be more excited to share this moment with you.”




https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1YEHOKYVTho




Big numbers for GTA 6 were always expected. Sensor Tower had been sharing unofficial sales data for GTA 6 for a long time already, but Take-Two's sales numbers are even higher than the 25 million sales that Sensor Tower reported at launch. 



GTA 6 is only going to get bigger when it comes to sales as more and more people buy the game. Additionally, GTA 6 is expected to come to PC in 2027, which will be another selling cycle for the game. Beyond this, GTA 6 is expected to add an online mode in 2027 that will no doubt feature microtransactions and other ways for Rockstar to make money off the fanbase.



For more, check out GameSpot’s GTA 6 review and our rundown of the five best things to do first. And if you’re eager for news on GTA 7? Get comfortable, because Rockstar is not going to announce it anytime soon.

articles.title: Echograph Is a Retro-3D Survival Horror Game That’s Equal Parts Resident Evil and Pokemon Snap
articles.title_tr: Echograph Is a Retro-3D Survival Horror Game That’s Equal Parts Resident Evil and Pokemon Snap
articles.summary: There's been a slow, steady revival of the styling of early 3D games. With the captivating look of low-polygon worlds – designed around clear technical limitations, but still brimming with craft – many indie games like Derelikt and Crow Country aimed to recreate the visual style and aesthetic of games from the console era of the PS1, Sega Saturn, and N64. In doing so, it gives new and returning generations of players an appreciation for the style of early 3D games. This is especially true for games looking to recreate the eeriness of that low-polygon aesthetic for new horror experiences, such as the upcoming Echograph.
